TRENDEFFICIENCYCONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_.summary: Retried US500's top-priority near-miss mechanism (trend-efficiency regime continuation, long side) on JPN. Passed Gate A, Gate C, AND the three-metric PBO MUCH more cleanly than on US500 (PBO=8.0% vs US500's 49.1%; Prob[OOS<=0]=20.0% vs 26.5%; both comfortably inside the 11-clean-live-edges range). Steps 01-03 all passed. But Gate D FAILS again: AUC=0.5089, p=0.2004 (Mann-Whitney, not significant), essentially identical to US500's AUC=0.5010.
TRENDEFFICIENCYCONTINUATION_LONG_KILLED_.cross_asset_finding: CRITICAL: this is the SAME mechanism, same Gate D failure mode, on a SECOND independent asset (US500 AUC=0.5010 p=0.4641; JPN AUC=0.5089 p=0.2004). This is much stronger evidence than a single-asset result that the failure is structural to the TRIGGER DESIGN (a binary 'is this bar in a clean-trend regime' gate), not asset-specific overfitting or population heterogeneity that a different asset's data would happen to fix. The event trigger itself has genuine average edge on both assets (confirmed via Gate A/C), but regime-level gating alone does not produce a population with enough internal cross-sectional variation for ANY meta-model trained this way to rank winners from losers. This mechanism (trend-efficiency / clean-trend regime continuation) should likely be considered STRUCTURALLY INCOMPATIBLE with meta-labeling as currently implemented, not just unlucky on two assets -- deprioritize retrying it again on NASDAQ/DAX/etc without first changing the underlying design (e.g. adding a continuous per-event differentiator, not just a cleaner trigger).
